stemMd: The second passage responds to the first chiefly by

options.label: A
options.textMd: denying that noise rules can be legitimate.

options.label: B
options.textMd: claiming schedules necessarily judge musical merit.

options.label: C
options.textMd: accepting its objection to artistic auditions while identifying another source of unequal access.

options.label: D
options.textMd: defending auditions as the only fair method.

options.label: E
options.textMd: arguing that cities should ban street performance.

explanationMd: The second begins with agreement and then broadens the design problem. Content neutrality does not guarantee practical access when application procedures favor established applicants.

distractorRationale.e: Both seek a fair permit system.
distractorRationale.b: The second distinguishes practical allocation from artistic judgment.
